examTips: For a body-part picture, name the **exact part**. Do not mix up an arm with a hand, or a leg with a foot.
Write a full sentence: **I see with my eyes.** Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
For handwashing, give the steps in **order**. Do not leave out washing **between the fingers**.
For odd-one-out questions, say each word aloud and listen to its **first sound**. When writing letters, check whether you need **capital** or **small** letters.
content.funFact: Your **nose** has two jobs in the poem: it helps you **smell** and **breathe**!

keyPoints.heading: Two Little Hands
points: Two **hands** clap. Two **legs** tap and walk. One **head** moves from side to side.
Two **eyes** look around and see. Two **ears** hear sounds.
One **nose** smells and helps us breathe. One **mouth** eats and talks. My body belongs to me.
Memory rhyme: Say “**clap, clap, clap**” and clap your hands. Say “**tap, tap, tap**” and tap your feet. Find the words **one, two, to** in the song.

keyPoints.heading: Name, Point and Speak
points: Sing and touch in order: **head, shoulders, knees, toes**. Then touch **eyes, ears, mouth, nose**. Touching each part helps you remember the song.
Say: I clap with my **hands**. I tap with my **feet**. I look with my eyes. I walk with my **legs**.
Nitin and Neha ask and answer. For one part, say “**This is my nose.**” For more than one, say “**These are my ears.**” Also practise with mouth, shoulders, hands and legs.
Match these names to pictures: **head, nose, eye, ear**; **cheek, hand, tongue, arm**; **mouth, foot, leg**. Point to each part as you say its name.

keyPoints.heading: Read, Draw and Wash
points: Read aloud: I see with my **eyes**. I hear with my **ears**. I smell with my **nose**.
I eat with my **mouth**. I feel with my **skin**. Finger trick: Raise one finger for each action—see, hear, smell, eat, feel. Name its body part.
Place one **palm** on the page. Draw its outline with your other hand. Decorate it with colours, paper bits or bindis. **Compare** it with your friend’s drawing.
Wash in order: Wet your hands → rub on **soap** → wash **between fingers** → rinse again. Picture trick: Imagine water, soap, finger gaps and water again. This helps you remember the four steps.

keyPoints.heading: Alphabet and Letter Words
points: Sing in chunks: **ABCDEFG**, HIJK, LMNOP; LMNOP, QRST, UVWXYZ. The song repeats **LMNOP**. Use this repeated chunk to remember the middle letters.
Practise writing the letters **A to F**. Match their big and small forms: **Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, Ee, Ff**.
Sing: a—ant, b—bag, c—cat, d—dog, e—egg, f—fish, g—goat, h—hut, i—ice-cube, j—jug, k—kite, l—lion, m—mango. Say each **letter** and its **word** together.
Continue: n—nose, o—orange, p—parrot, q—quilt, r—rat, s—sun, t—table, u—umbrella, v—van, w—well, x—x-ray, y—yarn, z—zebra. Picture trick: Imagine **yarn** beside a **zebra** to remember y and z.

keyPoints.heading: Listen to Letter Sounds
points: Say the words aloud: **a**—axe, ant, arm; **b**—bag, bee, boy; **c**—cart, cap, cat.
Continue: **d**—den, door, dog; **e**—egg, ear, elephant. Listen carefully to the **first sound** of each word.
Find the odd one out: bag, cap, balloon → **cap**; apple, ant, clock → **clock**; egg, dog, drum → **egg**. Each chosen word starts with a different sound from the other two.
Sound trick: Say “**b-b-bag, b-b-balloon**”. They start alike, but cap does not. Say “**d-d-dog, d-d-drum**”. They start alike, but egg does not.

keyTerms.meaning: All of **me**, including my head, arms and legs.
Bring your **hands** together to make a sound.
Hit lightly. In the speaking activity, we tap with our **feet**.
The part covering our body. We **feel** with our skin.
Use **water** to wash the soap away.
The **first sound** you hear in a word.
The word that is **different**. Here, listen for a different first sound.

quickRevision: Two hands **clap**. Two legs tap and **walk**. One head moves side to side. Practise reading one, two and to.
Say and point: **head, shoulders, knees, toes**. Also find your cheek, tongue, arm, hand, foot and leg.
Eyes **see**. Ears **hear**. The nose smells and breathes. The mouth eats and talks. Skin helps us **feel**.
Say: **This is** my mouth. **These are** my hands. For the hand activity, trace your palm, decorate it and compare it with your friend’s drawing.
Wash in order: put **water** on your hands, rub **soap**, wash between fingers and **rinse** again.
Sing **A to Z**. Match capitals and small letters: Aa, Bb, Cc, Dd, Ee, Ff. Remember i–ice-cube, j–jug, k–kite, l–lion, m–mango and n–nose.

content.summary: This chapter names our **body parts** and tells us what they do. We sing, point, clap and talk. We draw a hand and learn to **wash our hands**. We also sing the **alphabet** and listen to the first sounds of words.
content.title: Two Little Hands

tricks.explanation: This helps you remember the **body parts** and their numbers in the song.
tricks.title: Two and one
tricks.trick: Say **two** for hands, legs, eyes and ears. Say **one** for head, nose and mouth. Point as you say!

tricks.explanation: This picture helps you remember the **order** in the body song.
tricks.title: Touch and travel
tricks.trick: Imagine your fingers travelling down: **head, shoulders, knees, toes**. Touch each part as you sing.

tricks.explanation: Say this memory rhyme and point to each part. It links **eyes, ears and nose** to their jobs. It also reminds you what your mouth and skin do.
tricks.title: My body rhyme
tricks.trick: Eyes see, ears hear. Nose smells something near. Mouth eats a meal. **Skin helps me feel**.

tricks.explanation: Use **This is** for one body part. Use **These are** for more than one.
tricks.title: One nose, two ears
tricks.trick: Point to your nose: **This is** my nose. Point to both ears: **These are** my ears.

tricks.explanation: Remember the order: **water → soap → between fingers → rinse**. These are the four handwashing steps.
tricks.title: A soap adventure
tricks.trick: Imagine soap visiting your hands. First, water welcomes it. Then, rub the soap. It travels **between the fingers**. Rinse it away!

tricks.explanation: The pictures help you match **letters and words**. For an odd-one-out task, listen to the first sound: bag and balloon start alike, but cap does not.
tricks.title: Alphabet picture train
tricks.trick: Picture an alphabet train: **a–ant, b–bag, c–cat, d–dog, e–egg**. Later come q–quilt, w–well, x–x-ray and y–yarn. Say each letter and word.
